text:
rachel: Heads-up: our nightly linkcheck flagged some strange anchor mismatches coming from code snippets that include headings inlined. Example: https://docs.redwood.ai/examples/webhooks#payload-format doesn't jump because the snippet renders a `# Payload format` inside the included MD which becomes `payload-format-1`.

rachel: Repro steps: 1) open examples/webhooks 2) click left-nav link to Payload format 3) page loads but scroll fails (ends at top). Works if I open the page and search for 'Payload format' and click the second occurence.

tom: I saw this too after last week's include refactor. The include renderer preserves headings inside snippets, so duplicates get incremented (`-1`, `-2`). Our internal links were authored against the parent heading (no suffix).

anika: Two paths: strip headings when including snippets, or prefer explicit stable ids in the parent. Stripping headings might break example readability in isolation.

luke: Another wrinkle: some snippets are auto-generated by a tool and re-run in CI; adding explicit IDs there would get overwritten. We need a rule for generated snippets.

rachel: Idea: add a tiny preprocessor in the docs pipeline that, at build time, collapses duplicate ids by favoring the parent heading id and renaming included ones to suffix forms, and emit a warning with file paths. That way we avoid changing generated artifacts.

anika: That could work. Can your script also produce a `fixme.csv` that maps old links -> actual rendered id so content owners can opt-in to change later?

rachel: Yes. Prototype script attached in PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4520. Core of script: ```bash
# find duplicated ids in generated html
rg "id=\"[^\"]+-\d+\"" build/ -o --hidden | sed 's/id=\"//;s/\"//' | sort -u > duplicated_ids.txt
# map back to sources using the search index
python tools/map_ids_to_sources.py duplicated_ids.txt > fixme.csv
```

luke: Nice. Add a small unit test to the pipeline that fails if a link points to an id that ends in `-\d+` without a corresponding explicit parent id. That'll catch regressions.

deploy-bot: Preview build started for PR 4520 — linkcheck queued.

tom: Also found some SDK snippets where inline `<Component>` examples created stray headings when not escaped, causing more duplicates. I left a couple of comments on the PR to escape angle brackets or wrap them in backticks.

anika: For generated snippets, we should update the generator to add `<!-- allow-duplicate-heading -->` comment if heading is expected to be duplicated. Then the preprocessor won't warn for those. Luke, can you coordinate with the generator owners?

luke: Yeah I’ll open an issue in the generator repo and propose an `allow-duplicate-heading` opt-out flag. Meanwhile, the preprocessor will ignore files with that comment.

deploy-bot: Linkcheck completed: 1 warning (external), 0 failures. Script mapped 14 duplicated ids and created `fixme.csv` in the PR branch. Preview: https://deploy-preview-4520--docs.redwood.ai/examples/webhooks — anchor works for me now.

rachel: Merged PR 4520. I've added a short note to docs/contrib/includes.md describing the policy: prefer parent explicit ids for user-facing anchors; if snippet is generated, add `allow-duplicate-heading` opt-out and track the mapping in fixme.csv.

anika: Great. Follow-up: let's add a linkcheck rule to treat duplicated-ids as failures (not warnings) after Q2 so we enforce clean anchors. For now warn+report is okay while we sweep the repo.

luke: I'll take the generator issue and propose a small patch. Thanks y'all. :rocket:
